layoutData.body:
Ridgeline Metal Fabrication Inc. was founded in 1996 by Gord McAllister as Ridgeline Welding, operating from a rented bay in Leduc doing repair work. The company started fabrication work around 2001, building skid bases and hiring its first two journeymen. In 2005, Ridgeline landed Larkspur as a customer, marking the beginning of a 20-year relationship that continues today.

The company built its current 28,000 square foot facility in Nisku in 2008 and changed its name to Ridgeline Metal Fabrication in 2009 when adding structural steel work to its capabilities. In 2011, the company obtained CWB Division 2 certification, opening the door to more complex oil and gas fabrication projects.

Today, Ridgeline is a custom structural and miscellaneous steel fabricator and welding contractor serving three core markets: midstream oil and gas (pipe rack modules, compressor and meter skid bases, process module structural steel), agriculture (grain handling support structures, catwalks, conveyor galleries, barn steel, gates, custom farm structures), and commercial construction (structural steel packages, miscellaneous metals including stairs, rails, and embeds).

The company also provides field welding and repair services across central Alberta with three fully equipped welding trucks available for emergency call-outs. Products range from large fabricated assemblies such as pipe rack modules and grain elevator structures to precision components like launcher/receiver skids and equipment platforms.

Ridgeline employs 42 people and operates from a pre-engineered steel building in Nisku Industrial Business Park with three overhead cranes, modern CNC plasma cutting and beam processing equipment, and a 3-acre fenced and gravelled yard for assembly and staging.

left.title: Diversified Base with Deep Relationships
left.content:
Ridgeline has cultivated long-term customer relationships across multiple industry verticals, providing stability and recurring revenue. The company's flagship relationship is with Larkspur Midstream Services Ltd., a 20-year partnership where Ridgeline has never missed a delivery. This track record has earned the company consistently high vendor performance scores and repeat work on pipe rack modules, compressor skid bases, and structural steel packages for midstream facilities.

Beyond oil and gas, the customer base spans grain co-operatives (Prairie Crest Grain Co-operative), commercial construction firms (Bowline Construction Group), process systems integrators (Halvorsen), agricultural equipment manufacturers, mechanical contractors, and farming operations. This diversification across sectors mitigates cyclical risk inherent to any single industry.

Customers value Ridgeline's CWB Division 2 certification, clean quality record, and ability to deliver complex fabrications on schedule. The company is pre-qualified on Larkspur and Halvorsen vendor portals and undergoes annual audits from both customers with consistently clean results. Repeat business and referrals drive a significant portion of revenue, reflecting the strength of these relationships.

left.content:
Ridgeline operates from a fully equipped 28,000 square foot fabrication facility in Nisku, housing a modern mix of CNC-controlled fabrication equipment, welding systems, and material handling assets that support both custom structural fabrication and high-volume production work.

The centerpiece of the fabrication floor is a CNC high-definition plasma cutting table with bevel head, measuring 10 ft × 30 ft with 400-amp HD plasma and 45-degree bevel capability. Placed in service in 2024 at an original cost of $468,000, this system eliminates manual grinding on weld preps and dramatically improves cut quality and throughput on structural steel packages. The table is backed by a secondary CNC plasma cutting system (8 ft × 20 ft, 260-amp, acquired 2014) for smaller parts and overflow work.

Forming capacity includes a hydraulic CNC press brake rated at 230 tons × 12 ft with 6-axis control, purchased in 2019 for $312,000. An older hydraulic press brake (110-ton × 10 ft, 2-axis, 2011) remains in service but is nearing end of life and will require replacement in the next one to two years at an estimated cost of approximately $180,000.

The CNC beam drill and saw line, acquired in 2021 for $486,000, features a 3-spindle drill head, 44-inch maximum beam capacity, integrated bandsaw, and 120 ft of infeed and outfeed conveyor. This system is a key differentiator for structural steel work and was cited by the seller as a factor in winning Larkspur work.

Material handling is supported by three overhead bridge cranes: two 10-ton top-running units and one 5-ton under-hung crane, all installed in 2008. The two 10-ton cranes received a complete rebuild in summer 2024 at a cost of $64,000, including new hoists, new end trucks, and new pendants; the seller states these units will not require major work for another 20 years.

The welding department operates 28 multiprocess welding power sources (MIG, flux-core, stick, mixed vintages 2016–2024), 4 pulse MIG welders for aluminum and stainless with push-pull guns (2022), and a submerged arc welding tractor with column and boom manipulator (12 ft × 12 ft, 1,000-amp, 2020). A central welding fume extraction system with 6 ducted arms was installed in 2022.

Mobile assets include field service trucks (two one-ton pickups with welding decks and engine-driven welders, 2021 and 2023), a tandem-axle flatbed truck (26 ft deck, 2020), a service truck with 6-ton knuckle crane (2017), and yard equipment including two forklifts (15,000 lb diesel and 8,000 lb propane) and a telehandler (10,000 lb, 55 ft reach, 2019).

The seller notes that fully amortized tools, welders, and vehicles with an original cost of approximately $2,642,000 remain in operation and are carried at nil book value but continue to provide productive capacity.

items.title: ABSA Certification for Pressure Piping
items.description: Obtain ABSA pressure-piping QC program certification to capture piping fabrication work currently lost to competitors. Ridgeline presently refers out or declines packages containing pressure piping, limiting bid competitiveness on integrated oil and gas projects. ABSA certification would unlock additional revenue on existing customer base and enable pursuit of larger module contracts.

items.title: Robotic Welding Cell for Repeat Frames
items.description: Install robotic welding system for high-volume repeat customer frames, particularly Whitemud Ag Equipment opportunities. Automation would reduce cycle time on standardized weldments, improve margin consistency, and free journeyman capacity for complex structural work. Excellent fit for agricultural equipment support structures and conveyor components with recurring geometries.

items.title: Second Shift on CNC Equipment
items.description: Add second shift operation on beam line and plasma cutting tables to double throughput on fabrication preparation. Current equipment utilization at approximately 75% of one-shift capacity; both the CNC beam drill and saw line and the high-definition plasma table can run second shift immediately with two additional operators. Fitting and welding bays remain the bottleneck, not machine capacity.

items.title: Expand Fitting and Welding Capacity
items.description: Add fitting bays and welding stations in the existing 3-acre fenced and gravelled yard to alleviate the primary production bottleneck. Current 28,000 square foot shop focuses on enclosed fabrication; outdoor expansion would accommodate larger structural assemblies, seasonal ag work overflow, and module pre-fit operations. Space available for immediate deployment without real estate acquisition.

items.title: Larkspur Vendor Consolidation – 2026
items.description: Larkspur Midstream (18% of revenue, 20-year relationship) is reducing its approved fabricator list from 8 to 3 suppliers in 2026 and will re-bid the MSA. Ridgeline has maintained 100% on-time delivery over two decades, holds CWB Division 2 certification, and scores very well on vendor metrics (TRIF 1.1, strong quality). Management expects Ridgeline to make the short list, but the re-bid introduces execution risk during ownership transition.

items.title: Estimator Retention Risk
items.description: Devin (13 years with the company) is the chief estimator, pricing all jobs over $50,000 with deep knowledge of shop rates and fabrication times. He has no employment contract or non-compete and has not indicated whether he would stay under new ownership. Losing Devin would require slowing new bids and leaning on repeat customers for 3–6 months while a replacement is trained. Seller strongly recommends buyer discuss retention bonus on day one.

items.title: Senior Welder Retirements
items.description: Walt and Henry, two senior journeyman welders, are expected to retire in 2–3 years. The company has two fourth-year apprentices ready to replace them, but the Nisku journeyman hiring market is very difficult. Apprenticeship pipeline and low journeyman turnover (average ~9 years tenure, haven't lost a good journeyman to another shop in 5 years) mitigate immediate risk, but succession planning will be important.

items.title: Equipment Replacement Needs
items.description: The 110-ton hydraulic press brake (2011) leaks and has a manual back gauge; it needs replacement in 1–2 years at an estimated cost of ~$180,000. The older 8 ft × 20 ft CNC plasma table (2014) is on borrowed time. The 2016 forklift will also require replacement. Conservative capex forecast is $400,000 over the next 3 years. Recent investments (new $468,000 plasma table with bevel head, beam line, 230-ton brake, and both 10-ton cranes rebuilt in 2024) are in excellent condition for 10+ years.

items.title: Westlock Purchase Order Pending
items.description: The Westlock terminal expansion project is counted in the $3.1M signed backlog, but the purchase order has not yet been received. The project manager verbally awarded the work pending board approval (expected end of June 2025). Operations manager Luis will not order steel or begin fabrication until the PO is in hand, citing a prior loss from cutting material before PO on a different project. If the PO does not materialize, backlog would be reduced by the Westlock scope.

items.title: Coldbrook Payment Dispute
items.description: A trailer modification project completed in October 2024 for Coldbrook is subject to a payment dispute. The customer changed drawings twice but still wanted the same delivery date; Ridgeline was 5 days late. The receivable ($38,000, over 90 days) is with a collection agency. Payment status is uncertain.

items.title: Employee Retention Under Ownership Change
items.description: Employees value the current culture – the owner knows their kids' names. Retention of key staff (Luis operations manager, Tanya job costing, Mark QC, and the journeyman core) is critical through transition. Luis intends to stay post-sale and is open to rolling part of his 15% equity if the buyer has a good plan. Seller recommends buyer-funded retention plan for key staff, particularly Devin.

layoutData.body:
After 29 years of building Ridgeline Metal Fabrication from a single-bay repair shop into one of Alberta's most trusted structural steel fabricators, Gord McAllister is ready to retire. Since founding the business in 1996, Gord has built long-standing relationships with customers like Larkspur Midstream, invested in world-class equipment, and assembled a team of skilled journeymen welders and fabricators. Now he's looking to pass the torch to a buyer who will keep the shop in Nisku and continue the culture that has made Ridgeline successful.

Gord is committed to a smooth transition. He will work full-time for one year to personally introduce the new owner to every customer — Larkspur, Prairie Crest, Bowline, Halvorsen, and all the others. After that first year, he will remain available by phone as needed to support the new owner. This hands-on approach ensures that the relationships and operational knowledge that took nearly three decades to build are transferred effectively.

Luis Ortega, who has been with Ridgeline for 21 years and owns 15% of the company, intends to stay on as operations manager after the sale. Luis is a Red Seal journeyman welder, holds his CWB welding supervisor ticket, and manages the day-to-day shop operations. His continued involvement will be critical to maintaining continuity with the crew and customers. Luis is also open to rolling part of his equity into the new ownership structure if the buyer has a strong plan for the business, subject to consultation with his lawyer and family.

The buyer should plan to retain key personnel, particularly Devin Pritchard, the chief estimator who has priced jobs for Ridgeline for 13 years. A retention bonus for Devin and other key staff is recommended and should be buyer-funded. Gord's advice to any prospective buyer is straightforward: keep Luis, keep the location, and keep the team intact.

items.title: Training & Transition Support
items.description: Seller will provide one year full-time training including personal introduction to every customer (Larkspur, Prairie Crest, Bowline, all relationships). Available by phone thereafter as needed.

items.title: Retain Luis Ortega as operations manager
items.description: Luis Ortega (15% shareholder, 21 years with the company, Red Seal welder, CWB welding supervisor) intends to stay post-sale. Gord McAllister states that any buyer who does not keep Luis would be making a serious mistake. Luis is open to rolling part of his 15% equity if the buyer has a good plan and will consult his lawyer and wife. Luis manages day-to-day shop operations and maintains strong relationships with customers including Larkspur project managers.

items.title: Keep the Nisku shop location
items.description: The business operates from a 28,000 square foot facility on 3.1 acres in Nisku Industrial Business Park. The current lease expires December 31, 2026, with two five-year renewal options available. The building can be leased or purchased separately for $4,100,000. The location provides proximity to key customers and suppliers, with established infrastructure including three overhead cranes, 800-amp electrical service, and permitted paint booth.

items.title: Maintain the employee culture
items.description: Employees value that Gord McAllister knows their kids' names, reflecting a personal, family-oriented culture. Journeymen welders average approximately 9 years tenure. The company has not lost a good journeyman to another shop in 5 years. This culture has contributed to low turnover and strong operational stability. A buyer who preserves this environment will be better positioned to retain the skilled workforce.

items.title: Fund retention plan for Devin and key staff
items.description: Devin Pritchard (estimator, 13 years experience) is the biggest key-person risk after the owner. Devin prices all jobs over $50,000, knows shop rates and fabrication times, and has no contract or non-compete. The seller recommends the buyer discuss a retention bonus with Devin on day one. A retention plan for key staff is considered normal and should be buyer-funded. Other key personnel include Tanya (job costing and admin, 11 years) and Mark (QC inspector, 16 years, holds CWB welding supervisor ticket).

items.title: Understand the Larkspur relationship and 2026 re-bid
items.description: Larkspur represents 18% of 2024 revenue with a 20-year relationship and 100% on-time delivery record over that period. Larkspur is consolidating its approved fabricator list from 8 to 3 in 2026 and will re-bid the MSA. The seller is confident Ridgeline will make the short list based on its track record, CWB Division 2 certification, and beam line capability. Luis maintains strong relationships with Larkspur project managers. A successful buyer will need to navigate this re-bid process and demonstrate commitment to quality and delivery standards.

items.title: Plan for senior welder succession
items.description: Senior journeymen Walt and Henry are retiring in 2 to 3 years. The company currently has two fourth-year apprentices ready to replace them. The business takes 2 to 3 first-year apprentices annually from polytechnic and trains them in-house. A buyer should continue the apprenticeship program to maintain the skilled labour pipeline in a very difficult journeyman hiring market in Nisku.

items.title: Address equipment replacement needs
items.description: The 110-ton hydraulic press brake leaks and has a manual back gauge, requiring replacement in 1 to 2 years at an estimated cost of approximately $180,000. The old 8 ft x 20 ft plasma table from 2014 is on borrowed time. The forklift from 2016 will need replacement. A conservative capital expenditure forecast of $400,000 over the next 3 years covers these replacements. Recent investments including the new $468,000 CNC plasma table, beam line, 230-ton brake, and rebuilt cranes are in good condition for 10-plus years.
